structured_output.question: In short-schedule CNN training (about 10 epochs or fewer, CIFAR-scale 32px or ImageNet-scale fast runs), how much top-1 accuracy does progressive resizing cost at matched epochs? Here progressive resizing means training early epochs at lower resolution (e.g. 24px of 32px, 128 of 224) and finishing at full resolution. Which resolution schedule works best (number of stages, step vs smooth ramp, fraction of epochs at low resolution, when to switch to full resolution)? How is the train-test resolution discrepancy best handled: BN statistic recalibration, FixRes-style final fine-tuning at test resolution, ending with enough full-res epochs, and crop/scale augmentation coupled to resolution? Context: in our runs, 50% of epochs at 24px cut time 12-21% but lost 0.4-0.8 pp, and adding epochs did not fully recover it (E011, E015).
queries: progressive resizing image classification fast training
progressive learning image size regularization EfficientNetV2
mixed resolution training budgeted CNN low resolution early epochs
fast ImageNet training progressive resizing low resolution schedule
batch normalization statistics recalibration resolution change
rubric: Trains an image classifier from scratch with lower-resolution inputs in early epochs (progressive resizing, multi-stage or mixed resolution) and reports top-1 accuracy and/or wall-clock time against a fixed-resolution baseline at matched epochs or compute
Specifies or ablates the resolution schedule: the low-res sizes used, the fraction of epochs at low resolution, the timing of the final full-resolution phase, or step vs gradual ramp

Addresses the train-test resolution discrepancy, e.g. FixRes fine-tuning at test resolution, BN statistic recalibration, adapting augmentation strength or crop scale to resolution, or a final full-res phase
Preferably covers short or budgeted schedules (fast-training/speedrun regimes, <=~20 epochs, or a fixed time budget) on CIFAR, ImageNet or similar benchmarks
exclude: Papers without training-time experiments (pure inference or test-time resolution analysis with no retraining)
Methods that depend on pretrained weights or external data
Methods that rely on test-time augmentation or multi-scale test-time ensembles (TTA is banned)
Methods that use the test set for BN recalibration or tuning
